speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: One short. I have counted them, and I have counted them again. I am not accusing a name. I am saying the board is a spoon light, and I would like to know which of your callers has a taste for pewter.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Which caller, Mistress, is thought capable of making a profit from a spoon? I ask it politely. I would like the answer to be as particular as the charge.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: If I had the man, I would have the spoon. I have neither. Players come up your stair. A printer's boy has come. A brother has not come this month, which is almost a marvel. Pewter walks, Master Shakespeare. It does not fly.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I washed what was in the basin. The basin had its number. If one is gone, it went before the basin, or it never came to it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then it is in the house, or it has left the house. Those are the two countries. I live in the first of them today. I have not been out since church.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: After the week we have had, I was ready for an ordinary quarrel, and a spoon is the right size for one. I am not dressing it up. I am not making it Friday. A missing spoon is a missing spoon.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then let it stay a spoon. I am glad of a quarrel that fits in a kitchen. Search the kitchen before you search my callers. My callers are a long list, and a spoon is a small thing.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The ink-basket is still out from the morning. Mistress boils it on Mondays as a rule. The galls are in it, and the copperas, and the horn. I will look there before I look under a bed.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Look, then. And do not come back with a story about a caller if the story is only that you are tired of the floor.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It is here. In with the ink-things. Black to the neck. She has been measuring the galls and the copperas with it. Mistress, it is your own spoon.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Give it here.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Black to the neck. That is not a caller's pocket. That is a receipt. You sell the ink. You do not lose the measure and then hang it on my stair.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: It was put there to be found. Do not look so pleased about it. A woman may use the nearest spoon and forget the nearest spoon. That is not a theft. It is a Monday done on a Sunday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not pleased. I am relieved, which is a meaner feeling, and it will do. Put it on the board beside the ink-pot, where the next person who doubts you can see the colour of the doubt.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: On the board, then. Beside the pot. The black does not wipe with a thumb. It will have to soak. I am not scraping a good spoon into a bad one to save the look of it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Leave the black. I would rather see the stain than hear the accusation a second time. Master Shakespeare, your callers are restored to their characters. I accused nobody. I am accusing nobody now. Mark the difference.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I marked it the first time. You wondered which of them had a taste for pewter. You did not name one. The spoon has named the kitchen instead. I will take that as the end of it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I boil a fresh horn tomorrow, Mistress? This one has a spoon's worth of trouble in it, and the galls are low.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Tomorrow. Twopence the horn, if he wants it filled, and not a farthing off for being laughed at. Today the spoon goes on the board, and the house goes back to being a house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twopence tomorrow, if the horn wants filling. Not as a fine. As ink. I have plays enough this week to empty a horn, and I would rather buy it than borrow a spoon again.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will set it where you said, sir. Board, pot, and the stain showing. Then I am done with pewter for a Sunday.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Done is the right word. An ordinary quarrel, enjoyed, and finished. If you write it up into a bigger matter overnight, Master Shakespeare, I shall count the spoons in the morning out of spite.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not write it up. The spoon is found. The week we have just had can stay where it was. This kitchen is louder than that, and smaller, and I am glad of the size.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Glad is an odd word for a dirty spoon. I will take it. Glad is easier to wash than sorry.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Wash it in the morning. This afternoon it stays on the board, black to the neck, beside the pot, so I can see that I was the caller I was looking for.
